backlog.spec: Regularize the kernel member by training it on a noise-augmented copy of the data. After the quantile-normal scaling of the descriptors, build an augmented training set of 3 copies: the original Str plus 2 copies with independent Gaussian noise of sd 0.1 added to every feature, drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed), with the target tiled unchanged. Fit the same RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the ~2200-row augmented matrix and predict on the clean Ste. LightGBM and the 50/50 blend are untouched. The SVR cost grows roughly 9x but stays small.
backlog.title: Gaussian-noise augmentation for the SVR

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM member's constant leaves with linear models by setting linear_tree=True, linear_lambda=1.0 on the LGBMRegressor, keeping n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15 and the other settings. Before fitting, replace NaN and inf in the descriptor matrix by 0 as now and clip to a finite range so the leaf regressions stay stable. Keep the SVR member and the 50/50 blend exactly as they are. Only the tree structure of the LightGBM member changes.
backlog.title: LightGBM with linear leaves

backlog.spec: After fitting the LightGBM on the training descriptors, take its gain-based feature importances (model.booster_.feature_importance(importance_type='gain')). Keep only the 80 descriptors with the highest gain (among non-constant columns) as the SVR input, then quantile-normalize these and fit the same SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'). The selection uses training data only, inside fit_predict. LightGBM keeps all descriptors; the blend stays 50/50.
backlog.title: Top-importance feature selection for the SVR

backlog.spec: The SVR sees a skewed target; map it to a Gaussian before fitting. Inside fit_predict, fit a QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(200, len(y)), random_state=seed) on train_y reshaped to (-1,1), fit the RBF SVR (same C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the transformed target, then invert the transform on the SVR test predictions with inverse_transform before blending. LightGBM keeps the raw target. Keep the 50/50 average and the existing descriptor quantile scaling of the features unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-normal target transform for the SVR member

backlog.spec: After computing the blend 0.5*p_lgb + 0.5*p_svr, shrink the predictions toward the training median: final = med + s*(blend - med), where med = np.median(y) and s = 0.9. Apply the shrinkage only inside fit_predict on the returned array. Keep all models and their hyperparameters unchanged. The shrinkage is meant to reduce variance on unseen scaffolds, where predictions far from the mean tend to be the most wrong under a MAE loss. Set s as a module-level constant so it is easy to change.
backlog.title: Shrink blended predictions toward the training median

backlog.spec: In featurize, standardize each molecule before computing descriptors: use rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize to keep the largest fragment (LargestFragmentChooser) and then neutralize charges (Uncharger). If standardization fails, fall back to the original molecule. Silence RDKit logging with RDLogger.DisableLog('rdApp.*'). Compute all descriptors on the standardized molecule. Model, blend and hyperparameters stay the same.
backlog.title: Largest-fragment and neutralization standardization before featurizing

backlog.spec: For the SVR member only, fit on a transformed target: standardize y to z-scores, then map to ranks and to normal quantiles (scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n)). Map SVR predictions back by interpolating on the sorted training y values (np.interp over the sorted normal quantiles). LightGBM stays on the raw target. Keep the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Rank-normal target transform for SVR

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) for each training molecule. Count how many training molecules share each scaffold and set sample weight w_i = 1/sqrt(count_i), then normalize the weights to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to LGBMRegressor.fit and to SVR.fit (SVR accepts sample_weight). This stops large scaffold families from dominating the fit, which matters because the test folds are split by scaffold. Keep all other hyperparameters and the 50/50 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Inverse-density sample weights from scaffold cluster size

backlog.spec: In the SVR branch, replace the QuantileTransformer with sklearn.preprocessing.PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson', standardize=True) fitted on the kept descriptor columns of the training set (keep = Xtr.std(axis=0) > 0 as now). Apply transform to the test set. Before the transform, clip each descriptor column to the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training data to tame extreme values. Leave the LightGBM member, the SVR hyperparameters (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') and the 50/50 blend unchanged. Wrap the transform in a try/except that falls back to the existing quantile transform if the power fit fails to converge.
backlog.title: Yeo-Johnson power transform for SVR inputs instead of quantile normal

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with a bag of 15 SVRs. For each bag member i, draw a random 60% subset of the kept quantile-normalized descriptor columns with np.random.default_rng(seed + i), fit SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on those columns, and predict the test rows. Average the 15 predictions to form the SVR member. Keep the LightGBM member and the 50/50 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature-subset bagging of the SVR

backlog.spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest fragment by heavy atom count (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True, then max by GetNumHeavyAtoms) before computing descriptors. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: The ~210 RDKit descriptors include many near-useless columns that hurt the kernel member in particular. Fit one quick LightGBM (same hyperparameters, 200 trees) on the full training descriptors, rank columns by gain importance, and keep the top 80 columns. Re-fit the main LightGBM on those 80 columns and also restrict the SVR's quantile-scaled input to those same columns (intersected with the non-constant mask). Keep the 50/50 blend and everything else unchanged. Use random_state=seed for the selector fit so the selection is deterministic per fold.
backlog.title: Inner-CV feature selection by LightGBM importance

backlog.spec: Add a distance-weighted k-nearest-neighbour regressor as a cheap, low-bias third member. Reuse the quantile-normal-scaled descriptor matrix that already feeds the SVR (Str/Ste) and fit KNeighborsRegressor(n_neighbors=10, weights='distance', metric='euclidean', n_jobs=8) on it. Blend the three predictions with fixed weights 0.45 LightGBM, 0.45 SVR, 0.10 kNN. Nothing else changes; the kNN adds negligible runtime.
backlog.title: kNN as a third blend member

backlog.spec: Compress a structural fingerprint into a few dense columns so both members can use it without blowing up dimensionality. Compute 2048-bit hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048), GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), apply log1p, fit TruncatedSVD(n_components=32, random_state=seed) on the training fingerprints only, transform train and test, and append the 32 components to the RDKit descriptor matrix used by both LightGBM and the SVR (the SVR's quantile transform then covers the appended columns too). Keep the 50/50 blend and all model hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Add truncated-SVD components of atom-pair counts

backlog.spec: Replace the parallel 50/50 blend with residual stacking. Get 5-fold out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set (KFold with shuffle=True, random_state=seed, same LightGBM settings). Compute residuals y - oof. Fit the RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.05, gamma='scale') on the quantile-normalized descriptors to predict these residuals. Fit the LightGBM on the full training set for the test prediction. Final prediction = LightGBM(test) + 0.7 * SVR_residual(test).
backlog.title: SVR on LightGBM out-of-fold residuals

backlog.spec: Keep the LightGBM member's structure (500 trees, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10), but train it with a decaying learning rate. Pass callbacks=[lightgbm.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda it: 0.05 * (0.1 ** (it / 500)))] to fit, with the base learning_rate set to 0.05 so the rate falls from 0.05 to about 0.005 over the run. Import lightgbm.reset_parameter. Leave the SVR member and the 50/50 blend unchanged. The aim is a smoother late-stage fit with the same number of trees.
backlog.title: Learning-rate decay schedule for the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Append a small block of ionization features to the descriptor matrix (used by both LightGBM and the SVR): SMARTS-match counts for carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, phosphates/sulfonates (acidic groups); primary, secondary, tertiary aliphatic amines not adjacent to carbonyl, amidines, guanidines (basic groups); quaternary nitrogen. Derive from them: number of acidic groups, number of basic groups, estimated net charge (basic minus acidic), a zwitterion flag (both > 0), and a neutral flag. Also add TPSA/MolWt, HBD count / heavy atom count, and MolLogP - TPSA/50. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Charge-state and ionization features at pH 7.4

backlog.spec: For the SVR only, stack the quantile-normalized training matrix Str with 2 noisy copies (add N(0,0.15) noise with a seeded RNG) and replicate y accordingly. Fit the SVR (C=3, eps=0.1) on the augmented set. Keep LightGBM and the 50/50 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Gaussian-noise augmentation for SVR

memo: Helped: richer features and boosting. Descriptors plus Morgan counts cut loss from 0.4417 to 0.3917, and LightGBM gave 0.3722. The only accepted blend was LightGBM 50/50 with an RBF SVR on quantile-normalized descriptors (0.3650/0.3656, incumbent 0.3653). Did not help: model swaps (CatBoost 0.3894, 0.3682 as blend member; RF 0.3903; XGBoost 0.3808), pure SVR (0.3849), Tanimoto kernels (0.3764, 0.4176), GP (0.3690), MLP (0.3687), 3D shape (0.3675), SMARTS (0.3654), SVR retuning (0.3826, 0.3664). Within noise (sd ~0.0037): seed bagging (0.3646, 0.3653), learned blend weights (0.3635). Closest candidate: MACCS plus feature-Morgan counts (0.3599/0.3615 over 2 runs), rejected despite ~0.004 gain. Next: retry that feature addition in the blend, possibly with only LightGBM seeing it while the SVR keeps descriptors only. Replicate any gain under ~0.004. Avoid repeating seed bagging, blend weights, kernel swaps, SVR tuning, Huber.
